    #32236. Elly Griffiths’ 5 favorite female detectives in fiction

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1128 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Crimereads ↗ Open Full Page

    Elly Griffiths’ 5 favorite female detectives in fiction

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1128 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Crimereads

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that women have always solved crimes.
    • Recent findings suggest that it was some time, though, before crime-solving women appeared in print.
    • Recent findings suggest that interestingly, these first women sleuths were professionals, in that they earned their living from detection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that women have always solved crimes. I’m sure Eve knew immediately who killed Abel, although admittedly there was only one suspect. Grendel’s mother, in Beowulf, is one of the greatest justice-seekers in literature. The Wife of Bath would make a formidable sleuth, specializing in domestic cases.

    Recent findings suggest that it was some time, though, before crime-solving women appeared in print. In The Female Detective by Andrew Forrester (the pseudonym of James Redding Ware), published in 1864, Mrs Gladden is thought to be a dressmaker but is, in fact, a detective. The Revelations of a Lady Detective by William Hayward, also published in 1864, features Mrs Paschall, recruited by the Chief of Police to form a squad of women officers. In Mr Bazalgette’s Agent by Leonard Merrick, published in 1888, Miriam Lea is an aristocrat who becomes a private eye after falling on hard times.

    Recent findings suggest that interestingly, these first women sleuths were professionals, in that they earned their living from detection. The era of the talented but overlooked amateur, exemplified by Miss Marple, comes later.

    When I created forensic archaeologist Dr Ruth Galloway, I was drawing on the tradition of the civilian expert, often a woman, who assists the police. There many great unofficial detectives in modern crime fiction;  Freida Klein in Nicki French’s books, for example, or Rhona Macleod in Lin Anderson’s series. There are also many terrific women police officers: Val McDermid’s Karen Pirie, Sarah Hilary’s Marnie Rome, Nadine Matheson’s Anjelica Henley,  Jane Casey’s Maeve Kerrigan.

    Here are five of my favorite female detectives, official or otherwise.

    She’s not, strictly speaking, a detective but Marian Halcombe in The Woman in White by Wilkie Collins, is surely one of the greatest sleuths in crime fiction. Laura Fairlie is ostensibly the heroine but Marian, clever, brave and intrepid, is the beating heart of the book.

    Recent findings suggest that the Woman in White, published in 1859/60, is known as one of the great “sensation novels” and the sweeping narrative includes abduction, organized crime and murder. One of the most thrilling scenes has Marian clambering over rooftops at night in order to overhear a conversation between the villains Percival Glyde and Count Fosco. She’s in her petticoat because her voluminous silk skirt would have rustled too much. No wonder even evil Fosco is more than half in love with her.

    Sources indicate that no list would be complete without Agatha Christie’s famous spinster sleuth. Jane Marple was apparently inspired by the many unmarried women after the first world war, who, as they grew older, were often ignored by the world around them.

    It has been revealed that miss Marple, poised with rose clippers in her garden or bent over her crochet, makes the most of her invisibility. Almost every crime reminds Miss Marple of something she saw in her home village of St Mary Mead. She’s caustic, quietly brilliant and ruthless when on the trail of a murderer. In A Caribbean Mystery Jason Rafiel describes her as “Nemesis in a pink shawl.” Miss Marple is also surprisingly well-travelled, helped by a generous nephew and a doctor who is always happy to prescribe a holiday.

    In a recent development, I was delighted to be asked to contribute to Marple, a new collection of short stories featuring the divine Miss M. It was a daunting task made easier by the fact that we all think we know Miss Marple but she can still always surprise us.

    Ann Cleeves meant The Crow Trap to be a standalone novel. She was as surprised as anyone when, after a death at an isolated cottage in the Pennines, a rather unusual detective arrives to solve the case.

    Sources indicate that DI Vera Stanhope is “a large woman, amply covered” with a bulbous nose, man-sized feet and pitted skin. She’s scruffily dressed and carries a plastic bag containing her notes. She’s also brilliant, unconventional and frighteningly forthright. There are now thirteen Vera novels with a fourteenth, rumored to be the last, scheduled for 2027.

    Sources indicate that the TV series Vera, starring Brenda Blethyn as the eponymous detective, has run for fourteen seasons. Through the years we have learnt more about Vera’s history and her deep connection to the Northumbrian countryside but we can never second-guess our heroine who, like the similarly disheveled Columbo, always has the last word.

    Nancy Spain wrote six fantastically funny and atmospheric crime novels starring the indomitable Miriam Birdseye. I’m sure she would have gone on to write more if she hadn’t been killed in a  plane crash at the untimely age of forty-six. But in Miriam, Nancy has given us a detective for all time.

    Miriam is a  wildly glamorous “vaudeville star” whose modus operandi seems to be to get engaged to the prime suspect as promptly as possible. Miriam’s sidekick is the Russian ballerina, Natasha Nevkorina, whose ambition is to do as little as possible. Miriam is always prepared to dress up in the name of detection. Was there ever a better chapter heading than this, in Cinderella Goes to the Morgue–Enter Miriam, Disguised as a Principal Boy?

    It has been revealed that susie Steiner also left us tragically early, dying of a brain tumor in 2022. She only wrote three novels featuring DS Manon Bradshaw but she created one of my favorite modern detectives.

    Manon, named after the operatic heroine, is a terrific character: clever, kind, funny and often frustratingly stubborn. Manon’s relationships with her colleagues, Davy and Harriet, and, especially, with her adopted son, Fly, are beautifully described; full of warmth, nuance and humour. I’m sorry that there aren’t more novels about Manon, but this trilogy is crime-writing perfection.

    Stella Darnell first appears in The Detective’s Daughter by Lesley Thomson. Stella is the daughter of a police officer who died before he could solve his most important case. Stella had a complicated relationship with her father and has taken another path; she’s a cleaner.

    In a recent development, through the course of ten intricately-plotted books, Lesley Thomson charts how Stella, reluctantly at first, becomes a private detective whilst running her own cleaning agency. She solves crimes “stain by stain.” Along the way, Stella acquires a wonderful collection of assistants, including Jack Harmon, a tube driver who can sense murder….

    Recent findings suggest that elly Griffiths is the author of the Ruth Galloway and Brighton mystery series, as well as the standalone novels The Stranger Diaries, winner of the Edgar Award for Best Novel; The Postscript Murders; and Bleeding Heart Yard. She is the recipient of the CWA Dagger in the Library Award and the Mary Higgins Clark Award. She lives in Brighton, England.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Note, the release has been updated to include a quote from the National Security Division.

    According to recent reports, an eight-count superseding indictment was unsealed today charging Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, an Iraqi national, with terrorism-related offenses for their activities in support of Kata’ib Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), two U.S. designated foreign terrorist organizations (FTOs), including their involvement in nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks throughout Europe and the United States, and a September 2026 terrorist plot at a British Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, United Kingdom, where American armed forces were stationed.

    Recent findings suggest that “Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American servicemembers will be prosecuted by the United States government,” noted Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The defendants listed in the indictment allegedly supported two foreign terrorist organizations, and al-Saadi allegedly coordinated with his co-defendants in the days leading up to the attempted terrorist plot. This Department of Justice will continue dismantling terrorist networks and protecting the American people from terrorist organizations.”.

    It has been revealed that “This eight-count indictment reveals the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the U.S., including one plot that was recently prevented at RAF Fairfield, a British Royal Air Force Base where American forces were stationed,” remarked FBI Director Kash Patel. “According to the indictment, one of the subjects is behind bars awaiting trial yet he allegedly sent coded messages to assist in future acts of violence. To date, the subjects have been allegedly involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks throughout Europe and the United States in support of Kata’ib Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (“IRGC”), two U.S. designated foreign terrorist organizations. This FBI will use all our resources to detect and stop such terrorist attacks as we’ve done the last 21 months – with over 1,300 terrorists disrupted and nearly 7,000 Foreign Terrorist Organization related arrests, up 1,057%. All those who threaten our homeland will get the message – justice will find you.”.

    “Today marks a major disruption of an alleged global terrorism conspiracy,” mentioned Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “No matter where they are in the world, the National Security Division of the Department of Justice will pursue those who target American citizens and American interests. My thanks go out to the prosecutors and law enforcement partners for their work on this case.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “As alleged, these defendants helped orchestrate a campaign of terror on behalf of terrorist organizations affiliated with Iran that targeted Jewish communities in Europe and the United States, and the British military base, RAF Fairford, housing American service members,” mentioned U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of Fresh York. “Even after one of their co-conspirators was arrested and placed in federal custody, the defendants allegedly continued coordinating terrorist activity through coded communications and a network of associates overseas. The threat presented by Iran and Iran-backed terrorist groups to America and our allies is not hypothetical — it is very real. Our Office will not stop working to address and disrupt this threat, and to prosecute those responsible.”.

    Recent findings suggest that according to the allegations contained in the superseding indictment and other court filings: Al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri, and al-Hassani allegedly conspired to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the United States on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network, which included the IRGC and Kata’ib Hizballah, both of which are FTOs. Most recently, in approximately September 2026, al-Hassani allegedly orchestrated a terrorist plot at a British Royal Air Force Base (RAF Fairford) in Fairford, United Kingdom (the “RAF Fairford Terrorist Plot”), which at the time of the attempted attack, housed U.S. military aircraft and personnel.

    According to recent reports, al-Hassani and Mohajeri, both of whom were in Iran at the time of the RAF Fairford Terrorist Plot, allegedly relied on a network of contacts in the United Kingdom. Al-Saadi, who was imprisoned and awaiting trial on pending terrorism charges in the Southern District of Latest York, attempted to coordinate with al-Hassani and Mohajeri from jail by passing coded messages through third parties.

    Al-Saadi, a longtime operative of the IRGC and Kata’ib Hizballah, was charged in May for working with and on behalf of the IRGC and Kata’ib Hizballah, as well as other FTOs, for his involvement in planning and promoting approximately 18 terrorist attacks in Europe; and for attempting to bomb a synagogue in Fresh York. The picture below shows al-Saadi in front of an array of machineguns in a conference room with a map of the United States on the wall next to a list of “legitimate targets” (redacted here) identifying former and current U.S. officials.

    Sources indicate that as alleged, among the individuals with whom al-Saadi worked to facilitate and carry out the European Terrorist Attacks were Mohajeri and al-Hassani. Mohajeri is an Iranian national and operative of the IRGC who coordinated with al-Saadi and al-Hassani to carry out those terrorist attacks with the IRGC’s backing. Al-Hassani, who is originally from Iraq, used his contacts and criminal associates to carry out terrorist attacks in the United Kingdom.

    It has been revealed that the European Terrorist Attacks were carried out in the name of a purportedly newly introduced terrorist group with the pseudonym Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI), which is a front for Kata’ib Hizballah and other FTOs. Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the United Kingdom, the most of any European country. The attacks involved arsons, explosives, and in one instance, a near-fatal stabbing in London of two Jewish men, including a dual U.S.-British citizen.

    Recent findings suggest that al-Saadi, Mohajeri, and Al-Hassani were allegedly personally involved in planning many of the European Terrorist Attacks, and al-Saadi and Mohajeri helped create and publish online propaganda videos of these attacks. For example, on or about April 6, Mohajeri and al-Hassani planned attacks while together in a room in Iraq with a map of London displayed on a computer screen. In a video of that meeting, al-Hassani told Mohajeri, “we need to get focused on London.”  An image of the video is below, with Mohajeri on the right and al-Hassani on the left. HAYI then claimed responsibility for six terrorist attacks that occurred in and around London starting approximately one week later.

    On or about April 17, al-Saadi, al-Hassani, and Mohajeri allegedly directed an individual to carry out one of the European Terrorist Attacks in real time. Specifically, al-Saadi, al-Hassani, and Mohajeri, along with others, were in a room watching a FaceTime video with the individual who was carrying out the attack, which was projected onto a large screen against the background of the HAYI logo. Al-Hassani directed the perpetrators’ actions, including by instructing the individual on the other end of the call to execute the attack and directing that individual to take a lighter and “light one in your hand,” “light it,” and “throw the fourth one.” Al-Saadi recorded the attack in real time, while Mohajeri recorded al-Hassani and al-Saadi in the room as they directed the attack. A still image from Mohajeri’s recording, showing al-Saadi (circled in red) and al-Hassani (circled in green), as they directed and filmed the attack, is below.

    The next day, on or about April 18, al-Hassani participated in another video call with an individual carrying out an attack on a synagogue in London, with the HAYI logo projected on the background of al-Hassani’s screen. During the video call, al-Hassani directed the individual to “light it up like a Christmas tree.” The person on the video then lit an improvised explosive device and threw it at a building. An image from the video is shown below.

    In March and April — overlapping with the time that al-Saadi was co-located in Iraq with Mohajeri and al-Hassani, planning the European Terrorist Attacks — al-Saadi allegedly attempted to coordinate and carry out terrorist attacks in the United States, including by targeting a synagogue in Manhattan.

    On or about May 1, following the European Terrorist Attacks, al-Saadi was arrested abroad and subsequently transferred to the custody of the United States to face prosecution. Al-Saadi has been in federal custody since his arrival in the United States. For approximately four months following al-Saadi’s arrest, there were no additional attacks attributable to al-Saadi, Mohajeri, and al-Hassani.

    According to recent reports, in August, however, al-Hassani allegedly directed and paid associates in the United Kingdom to conduct preparatory steps and arrange logistics for the RAF Fairford Terrorist Plot. On Aug. 22, al-Hassani paid one individual (Individual-1) to perform pre-operational surveillance of RAF Fairford’s perimeter and al-Hassani subsequently received videos of the area surrounding the base. In later communications with al-Hassani, Individual-1 referred to him as “Ali.”.

    In September, al-Hassani also tasked and paid several individuals to help him prepare for the plot, including by procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel. At al-Hassani’s urging, those individuals commissioned custom decals that they affixed to the vans to create the appearance that they were used by a fuel delivery business and a swimming pool supply business.

    It has been revealed that on Sept. 26, al-Hassani allegedly tasked individuals to drive three vans, some of which were later determined to contain barrels of fuel, to the RAF Fairford base. That day, al-Hassani was in frequent communication with the van drivers, helping to coordinate their movements and directing them where to drive. At least two of the three vans, while en route to the perimeter of RAF Fairford, encountered a security roadblock and were not allowed to proceed on their intended route. Al-Hassani communicated with the drivers and occupants of the vans both before and after encountering the security checkpoint. In the early morning hours of Sept. 27, law enforcement authorities in the United Kingdom recovered three white vans to which the fuel delivery business logos were affixed and arrested the occupants.

    While in prison in Latest York awaiting trial, al-Saadi has had phone calls with his immediate family members located in Iraq. As alleged, al-Saadi used those calls to pass coded messages to Mohajeri and al-Hassani in the days leading up to the RAF Fairford Terrorist Plot.

    For example, in June and July, al-Saadi allegedly spoke with his mother and sister about Mohajeri. During those calls, they referred to Mohajeri by various aliases, including “Abbas, Abu Daniel” and “Sayyid Abbas.”  Al-Saadi also told his family members that he owed money to Mohajeri and directed them to pass along messages to Mohajeri about “work,” a term al-Saadi regularly used to describe terrorist activity, including on social media posts and in discussions with Mohajeri about partnering to conduct terrorist attacks. On one of those calls, al-Saadi also asked his sister, “What are they doing about all our old work?” and asked her whether it had been cancelled or just put on pause. Al-Saadi’s sister responded that “it isn’t cancelled.”.

    On or about Sept. 24, al-Saadi once again spoke with his immediate family by phone. On the call, al-Saadi allegedly inquired about how al-Hassani, whom al-Saadi referred to as “Ali,” was doing. Al-Saadi’s family informed al-Saadi that “Ali” had been transferred to the “International Section.”  Al-Saadi then allegedly instructed his family to “give him [al-Hassani] money so we can do it.”  As described above, three days later, al-Hassani orchestrated the RAF Fairford Terrorist Plot.

    Al-Saadi, 32, is a citizen of Iraq and Iran. Mohajeri, 48, is a citizen of Iran. Al-Hassani, 35, is a citizen of Iraq. A chart containing the names, charges, and minimum and maximum penalties for the defendants is set forth below.

    According to recent reports, the Justice Department praised the outstanding investigative work of the FBI’s New York Joint Terrorism Task Force, which consists of investigators and analysts from the FBI, the NYPD, and over 50 other federal, state, and local agencies, and the FBI Washington Field Office, Counterterrorism Division, as well as the assistance of the Department of Justice’s National Security Division, Counterterrorism Section, the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the NYPD, the New York State Police, and the Department of State.

    In a recent development, assistant U.S. Attorneys Jeffrey W. Coyle, Sarah L. Kushner, David J. Robles, and Chelsea L. Scism for the Southern District of Latest York are prosecuting the case, with assistance from James Donnelly and Paul Casey of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section.

    #32234. Christina Henry on translating the unexpected horrors of motherhood into fiction

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1390 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Crimereads ↗ Open Full Page

    Christina Henry on translating the unexpected horrors of motherhood into fiction

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Crimereads

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We all have a picture in our head of a mother—what we think a mother should be or shouldn’t be, what ideal motherhood looks like.
    • But being a mother, or a stepmother, or a mother figure, is hard.
    • In a recent development, once your child is born you might think, Great, it’s going to be nothing but sunshine and roses from here on out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We all have a picture in our head of a mother—what we think a mother should be or shouldn’t be, what ideal motherhood looks like. Society creates expectations for mothers, and mothers who color outside those lines are often censured by those around them.

    But being a mother, or a stepmother, or a mother figure, is hard. If you carry a child you might think that pregnancy will be nine months of glowing, radiant bliss (that’s what all those parenting influencers say on TikTok, don’t they?) Instead, you’re coping with swollen feet and sciatica, and the constant worry that you might do something that will accidentally harm your growing baby.

    In a recent development, once your child is born you might think, Great, it’s going to be nothing but sunshine and roses from here on out. But parenting isn’t just drippy ice cream cones on the beach and smiling while riding carousels. There are so many things you can’t anticipate—unexpected illnesses, trouble at school, headstrong kids who simply want their own way.

    Industry observers note that the truth of the matter that having a child and raising a child are often some of the most anxiety-riddled years of a person’s life. Even when nothing’s going wrong, a mother can often feel like something just might go wrong. The worry they are feeling is somehow a hedge against bad things happening—parental anxiety as a shield against actual harm.

    According to recent reports, fictional mothers, of course, get the worst of it. It’s bad enough that real-world mothers have to cope with spiking fevers and school permission forms and judgmental in-laws. But what if you desperately want a child but it turns out your baby was also, say, the son of Satan? Or what if you love your children with all your heart but you keep hearing things, seeing things that you aren’t sure are actually there? What if the people around you aren’t to be trusted? What if you feel like you can’t trust yourself?

    In a recent development, everyone knows about Rosemary, right? Poor Rosemary Woodhouse, whose gaslighting jerk of a husband, Guy, trades her womb for a successful career.

    In Ira Levin’s classic novel of motherhood horror, Rosemary’s Baby, Rosemary is a cheery newlywed who wants to have a child. Guy is a struggling actor who keeps just missing his big break and wants to wait a little longer to start a family. A bit of timely luck allows them to sign a lease in an older building called the Bramford, a place that’s notoriously difficult to get into. Rosemary is thrilled that, at least, she will have the decoration of a fresh place to keep her busy, but she still wishes for a baby.

    In a recent development, an older couple, Roman and Minnie Castavet, live in the next apartment. Rosemary finds them nosy and annoying, but for some reason Guy likes them and starts to visit regularly. Then, a miracle happens. The actor who cast in a role that Guy almost got is suddenly struck blind (a miracle for Guy, of course, not so much for the other actor) and Guy lands a role that can make his career. Soon after this unexpectedly fortuitous occurrence, he decides that he does, in fact, want a baby.

    Shortly after, Rosemary has a terrible dream—a dream about a beast who rapes her while several people look on. And then, the second miracle happens. Rosemary is pregnant. Except her pregnancy doesn’t feel right, and everyone around her keeps telling her it’s fine.

    Industry observers note that rosemary’s journey is so harrowing because no matter what she says or does or even knows with absolute certainty, no one will believe her. If you’ve never read this one it’s time to give it a try.

    Kit Burgoyne’s The Captive is a clever play on the I’ve-been-impregnated-by-Satan-against-my-will story, or in this case, by an entity alternately referred to as “The Long-Before” or “Him.” An underground revolutionary group that call themselves the Nail decide to kidnap Adeline Woolsaw, the wealthy heiress of a vast network of connected businesses, in hopes of exposing the Woolsaws and their corruption to the public. The only time Adeline ever seems to leave the vast estate where she lives is to go to the doctor’s office, so the group decides to grab her as she leaves her appointment.

    Unfortunately for the Nail, Adeline is pregnant. Even more unfortunately, Adeline is going into labor in the van. Just to add to their confusion, Adeline most definitely does not want to return home to her parents. It seems that her parents worship this evil entity and arranged to have Adeline carry His child in order to establish total world domination.

    This pitch-black story skewers the cultists, the radical revolutionaries and the oligarchs that run everything equally and mashes it all up into a super-fun (and frequently gory) thriller.

    It has been revealed that helen Phillip’s The Need is probably one of my favorite novels of the last ten years. I’ve never read another book that so accurately embodies both the intense love of a mother for her children and also the profound, dragging monotony of the daily tasks that make up her day.

    Molly is a mom of two and a paleobotanist, alone with the kids while her partner travels. She is exhausted, exhausted in that bone-deep way parents often are, feeling like she wants to stay on top of everything but she simply cannot.

    In a recent development, when she hears footsteps in her home she thinks she’s imagining them. She’s anxious about a potential home invasion. She can’t trust herself. She’s just sleep-deprived. But then she comes face to face with an intruder wearing a mask, and the reality of Molly’s world tilts precariously on its side.

    The less you know about this one, the better. It unfolds like a strange and fascinating puzzle box, revealing layers as it goes.

    Industry observers note that neena Viel’s debut Listen to Your Sister isn’t about a mother, per se. But it is about Calla Williams, a twenty-five-year-old woman just trying to keep it together, who reluctantly agrees to become the guardian to her sixteen-year-old brother Jamie. Jamie, like most 16-year-olds, is not interested in his sister’s authority, or any kind of authority, really. Their brother Dre agreed to help Calla with Jamie, but he has his own struggles and isn’t exactly present.

    It has been revealed that calla keeps trying, keeps sacrificing, keeps muddling along trying to do her best like every mother figure. Ever since her brothers were young she’s had visions of their dying in horrible ways, and her nightmares stoke her anxiety over their well-being. But her resentment is growing. No matter how much she loves her brothers, they don’t seem to love her enough to change.

    One day Jamie’s behavior goes a little too far and the siblings are forced to flee their homes to hide out at a cabin in the woods. It’s there that Calla’s patience finally snaps, and her brothers discover that the nightmares Calla has had all their lives might just be real.

    Sources indicate that neena Viel’s writing is so intense, so profoundly visual, that this book has been indelibly imprinted on my brain. I’m still thinking about it months later.

    In my own upcoming novel Pinfeathers, stay-at-home mom Nora Pacetti is tired and frustrated that her husband, Adam, isn’t keeping up his end of the parenting bargain. But those problems seem trivial once Nora discovers a strange object sticking out of her baby’s arm.

    Sources indicate that nora thinks it must be a splinter. But when she examines it closely the object seems to have come through her daughter’s skin, not pierced it from the outside. Then Nora’s mother Giulia looks at it and renders her verdict—it’s a pinfeather, a baby feather.

    According to recent reports, nora doesn’t know what to believe, and then she finds another one. Does her daughter have a strange disease, or is she actually turning into a bird?

    Christina Henry is the author of The Mermaid, Lost Boy, Alice, Red Queen, and the national bestselling Black Wings series featuring Agent of Death Madeline Black and her popcorn-loving gargoyle, Beezle.

    In a recent development, miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz at a U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing in Washington, D.C., on April 30, 2025. (Photo by Annabelle Gordon/Sipa USA/Sipa via AP Images).

    In a lawsuit that could affect how some forfeitures are handled in Florida, the Miami-Dade County sheriff is being accused of unconstitutionally allowing a law firm to profit when police seize property and cash.

    Under federal and state forfeiture law, police departments can seize money or assets, such as boats, that they think were used in crimes or purchased with ill-gotten gains.

    Mobile phone distributors and retailers in Miami argue that a firm run by Israel “Izzy” Reyes—a former cop, a former prosecutor and a former judge—is representing the sheriff’s office in civil forfeiture cases and keeping 20% to 35% of the proceeds, plus an additional 5% on appeal.

    According to court papers filed in October, the companies noted their bank accounts were frozen last year, and more than $45.2 million was seized as as part of civil forfeiture cases handled by the firm.

    An additional $2.6 billion has also been targeted for seizure, the companies alleged, according to a story by the Miami Herald.

    Rosie Cordero-Stutz is the first elected sheriff in Miami-Dade County since the 1960s.

    Breaking: Justice Department Announces Actions to Disrupt North Korea’s Massive Theft of Cryptocurrency

    📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1278 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fbi

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Today the Department of Justice unveiled coordinated actions against the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea (DPRK) government’s schemes to fund its regime through the massive theft of cryptocurrency.
    • “North Korea’s government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M.
    • Sources indicate that “The Criminal Division, specifically the Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), and our law enforcement partners played the critical role in immediately freezing billions of dollars’ worth of stolen Binance digital assets before they got beyond law enforcement reach,” remarked Assistant Attorney General A.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Today the Department of Justice unveiled coordinated actions against the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea (DPRK) government’s schemes to fund its regime through the massive theft of cryptocurrency. These actions include the seizure of cloud-based infrastructure used in the FaceStealer social engineering scheme that has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million worth of cryptocurrency and the court-authorized seizure and restraint of more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency recently stolen from Binance, a virtual currency exchange.

    “North Korea’s government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “Today’s announcement demonstrates that America will fight back against that corrupt regime’s effort to profit through cybercrime. The National Security Division will use every tool at its disposal to seize and return North Korea’s ill-gotten gains.”.

    Sources indicate that “The Criminal Division, specifically the Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS), and our law enforcement partners played the critical role in immediately freezing billions of dollars’ worth of stolen Binance digital assets before they got beyond law enforcement reach,” remarked Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “As the Department’s liaison to the digital asset industry, the Criminal Division promptly and efficiently used its expertise to immediately halt about half of this historic breach.”.

    “Cryptocurrency unfortunately has become fertile ground for North Korea to defraud victims and fund its malign activities,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “Today’s seizure shows that America will continue the fight against rogue states who financially gain from cybercrime.”.

    “By springing into action at a moment’s notice, we worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks,” remarked U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia. “The North Korean regime may think they are sophisticated cyber criminals, but we have consistently met them head on, as we did here seizing more than $1.2 billion of their stolen assets.”.

    “The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years,” stated FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman. “North Korean cyber actors have used the FaceStealer scheme to aggressively target individuals in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors through deceptive social engineering tactics, resulting in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months. The FBI remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and imposing cost on North Korean actors targeting the virtual asset community.”.

    “North Korea’s FaceStealer is a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user” stated Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy of the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office. “It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships. If you can’t imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough. The FBI is sounding the alarm to elevate awareness of this growing scheme, now aimed not only at crypto theft, but also the exploitation of the of the open-source software supply chain.”.

    Seizure of FaceStealer Infrastructure – Central District of California.

    Industry observers note that today, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California revealed the disruption of cloud-based infrastructure used by North Korean hackers in a highly effective social engineering scheme that the FBI is calling “FaceStealer.” The scheme, which relies on surreptitiously recorded videos and artificial deepfakes, has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months and the attempted compromise of individuals involved in the open-source software supply chain.

    North Korean hackers known publicly by the names Sapphire Sleet, UNC1069, Dangerous Password, CryptoCore, Advanced Persistent Threat 38 (APT38), BlueNoroff, and Stardust Chollima have lured targets with invitations to video meetings delivered from accounts stolen from prior victims. Once a target joins the meeting, the hackers record the target’s webcam video and play a prerecorded video of a previous victim or victims known to the target, thereby simulating the participation of trusted contacts in the meeting to gain the target’s trust. The North Korean hackers also use super intelligence (SI) to develop deepfake videos of well-known and influential individuals often in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries that make the FaceStealer scheme even more effective. Here again, they use the deepfake videos in the meetings with targets to gain the target’s trust.

    Recent findings suggest that during the meeting, the hackers then introduce a fake technical error into the meeting, such as claiming that the target cannot be heard, and provide a link or prompt to fix the error. The “fix” surreptitiously installs malware on the target’s computer. With the target’s computer compromised, the hackers can steal cryptocurrency or exploit the target’s access to other computer infrastructure. In several reported cases, the hackers stole cryptocurrency and hijacked communication accounts several months to more than a year after the initial compromise. As part of the scheme the hackers also accessed the new victim’s contact lists, social media, and communications apps to target the victim’s personal and professional contacts.

    The North Korean hackers target individuals working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries. Additionally, they have increasingly targeted individuals involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software with the FaceStealer technique, attempting to gain access to their devices and the software repository accounts they control. This targeting appears calculated to enable software supply-chain attacks. Pursuant to a federal warrant, the FBI seized over 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims.

    Sources indicate that the FBI today published a report providing greater detail on the mechanics of the FaceStealer scheme, including best practices to protect against this scheme and steps victims can take in the event of a compromise. Additionally, the FBI created a website, www.fbi.gov/facestealer, to serve as a centralized hub for resources and information on the scheme.

    The effort to disrupt the FaceStealer campaign was led by Assistant U.S. Attorney Khaldoun Shobaki for the Central District of California and the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office.

    The Department, FBI, and Law Enforcement Partners Interdict More Than a Billion Dollars Worth of Virtual Assets Stolen From Binance.

    In a recent development, separately from the FaceStealer campaign, on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as “TraderTraitor” stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange. Since the theft, the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section, the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, and law enforcement partners have worked closely with virtual asset service providers (VASPs) to interdict the stolen assets. Collective U.S. government and private sector efforts so far have resulted in the freeze of more than $2.7 billion, with the Department having already obtained court-authorization to seize or restrain in excess of $1.2 billion of that amount.

    Efforts to trace, freeze, seize, and forfeit the stolen virtual assets are ongoing, as TraderTraitor actors continue to launder such assets through various cryptocurrency bridges, mixers, and exchanges. For example, last week, the FBI, in coordination with its law enforcement partners at the U.S. Secret Service (USSS) and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS-CI), issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft and urging VASPs to block transactions with or derived from cryptocurrency addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder the stolen Binance assets.

    The FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, Cyber Division, and Virtual Asset Unit are coordinating the FBI’s efforts to recover the stolen virtual assets, working in partnership with the USSS and the IRS-CI.

    In a recent development, jimmy Harold Spurger Jr., 54, the chief investigator for the Dallas County public defender’s office, was arrested and charged with first-degree murder Saturday after his wife was found dead in their apartment. (Photo from the Dallas County Sheriff’s Department).

    The chief investigator for the Dallas County public defender’s office was arrested and charged with first-degree murder Saturday after his wife was found dead in their apartment.

    Jimmy Harold Spurger Jr., 54, who has worked for the public defender’s office for nearly 14 years, was married to his wife, Maria Teresa Spurger, for 35 years but filed for divorce in late October, according to Fox 4.

    Recent findings suggest that local first responders who were conducting a welfare check Friday night forced their way into the apartment, where they found Spurger’s wife unresponsive on a couch with a knife in her neck, Fox 4 reports. Spurger also was found in the apartment, covered in blood and sitting next to a knife in the bedroom.

    Recent findings suggest that after responding officers found multiple pill bottles also covered in blood, they suspected that Spurger had ingested pills and transported him to the hospital, Fox 4 reports. He was later taken into custody and is being held on a $1 million bond.

    Spurger has led the Investigative Division for the Dallas County public defender’s office for 11 months, Fox 4 reports. Previously, he spent more than 13 years in its Capital Murder Division. He also worked for more than 20 years in law enforcement, which included supervising investigations in the Child Abuse and Family Violence Division of the Dallas County district attorney’s office.

    Dallas County Chief Public Defender Christi Dean told Fox 4 that Spurger was “an exemplary colleague,” and that “it’s hard to imagine that he has been charged with murder.”.

    It has been revealed that “We know in our profession that the probable cause affidavit doesn’t tell the whole story,” Dean also reportedly said. “The media reports don’t tell the whole story. And we’re still in preliminary stages.”.

    • Viking Holdings today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on bookings.
    • “We delivered strong third quarter revenue, supported by continued fleet expansion, the benefits of our diversified business model and growth in revenue per PCD,” remarked Leah Talactac, President and CEO of Viking.
    • “While prolonged periods of historically low water levels disrupted portions of our European river operations during the quarter, our nearly 30 years of experience operating on Europe’s waterways allowed us to adapt to changing conditions and minimize the impact on our guests.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Viking Holdings today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on bookings.

    “We delivered strong third quarter revenue, supported by continued fleet expansion, the benefits of our diversified business model and growth in revenue per PCD,” remarked Leah Talactac, President and CEO of Viking.

    “While prolonged periods of historically low water levels disrupted portions of our European river operations during the quarter, our nearly 30 years of experience operating on Europe’s waterways allowed us to adapt to changing conditions and minimize the impact on our guests. We are proud of and thankful for our crew and shoreside teams for their extraordinary efforts during this period. Importantly, we remain encouraged by the resilience of demand across our diverse portfolio of products and the long-term appeal of the one Viking brand.”.

    Third Quarter 2026 Consolidated Results.

    During the third quarter of 2026, Capacity PCDs increased by 10.2% over the same period in 2025. This year-over-year increase was mainly driven by the growth of the Tech giant’s fleet. Occupancy for the third quarter of 2026 was 91.3% compared to 96.0% in 2025.

    Total revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $2,184.2 million, an increase of $184.6 million, or 9.2%, compared to the same period in 2025 mainly driven by increased Capacity PCDs and higher revenue per PCD in 2026 compared to 2025, partially offset by lower Occupancy.

    Gross margin for the third quarter of 2026 was $855.3 million, a decrease of $26.4 million, or 3.0%, compared to the same period in 2025, and Adjusted Gross Margin for the third quarter of 2026 was $1,388.1 million, an increase of $54.4 million, or 4.1%, over the same period in 2025. Net Yield was $612 for the third quarter of 2026, down 0.8% year-over-year.

    For the third quarter of 2026, vessel operating expenses were $461.4 million and vessel operating expenses excluding fuel were $401.2 million. Compared to the same period in 2025, vessel operating expenses increased $69.2 million, or 17.6%, and vessel operating expenses excluding fuel increased $54.7 million, or 15.8%, mainly driven by the growth of the Company’s fleet in 2026 compared to 2025.

    Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was $498.4 million compared to $514.0 million for the same period in 2025. Adjusted Net Income attributable to Viking Holdings Ltd was $496.9 million compared to $533.8 million for the same period in 2025.

    Adjusted EBITDA was $673.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $30.0 million, or 4.3%, over the same period in 2025.

    Diluted EPS and Adjusted EPS were $1.11 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to Diluted EPS of $1.15 and Adjusted EPS of $1.20 for the same period in 2025.

    Historically low water levels on certain European rivers impacted portions of the Company’s river operations during the third quarter of 2026. The Company implemented a range of mitigation measures to maintain operations and did not cancel any scheduled cruises. However, the low water conditions resulted in itinerary disruptions and increased guest cancellations, which reduced Occupancy compared to the third quarter of 2025. The low water disruptions reduced third quarter total revenue by approximately $100 million. The Company estimates that the impact on Adjusted Gross Margin was also approximately $100 million, reflecting the lost margin from guest cancellations as well as incremental direct costs incurred to mitigate the disruptions.

    Enhancement on Operating Capacity and Bookings.

    For our Core Products, operating capacity is 7% higher for the 2026 season compared to the 2025 season and 15% higher for the 2027 season compared to the 2026 season.

    As of November 8, 2026, for our Core Products, we had sold 93% of our Capacity PCDs for the 2026 season and 68% for the 2027 season.

    As of November 8, 2026, for our Core Products, we had $6,200 million of Advance Bookings for the 2026 season, 11% higher than the 2025 season at the same point in time. Since our last earnings release, Advance Bookings for the 2026 season declined primarily reflecting guest cancellations related to itineraries disrupted by low water levels. Advance Bookings per PCD for the 2026 season was $830, 6% higher than the 2025 season at the same point in time.

    Recent findings suggest that as of November 8, 2026, for our Core Products, we had $5,829 million of Advance Bookings for the 2027 season, 17% higher than the 2026 season at the same point in time. Advance Bookings per PCD for the 2027 season was $929, 8% higher than the 2026 season at the same point in time.

    The Company issued vouchers as a goodwill gesture to certain guests who traveled on itineraries impacted by low water levels. Advance Bookings include redemptions of vouchers. When a voucher is redeemed, the latest booking is reflected in Advance Bookings at net value.

    Recent findings suggest that “Our Advance Bookings remain strong, with 68% of our capacity for the 2027 season already sold, providing meaningful visibility into future demand,” remarked Linh Banh, Chief Financial Officer of Viking. “The enduring appeal of the Viking brand and our products, combined with our diversified business model, differentiated marketing capabilities and strong guest loyalty, continue to support our growth and reinforce our confidence in the long-term opportunities across our business.”.

    On September 10, 2026, the Manufacturer announced that its Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $1.0 billion. During the third quarter of 2026, the Company returned $350.0 million to shareholders through share repurchases.

    Since our second quarter 2026 earnings release, the Firm:.

    Based on the committed orderbook, the Organization expects to take delivery of one ocean ship and two river vessels during the remainder of 2026.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Asif Merchant, 48, of Pakistan, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Eric R. Komitee to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire. Merchant is a trained operative of the Iranian government’s global terrorist force, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Merchant was convicted by a federal jury in March 2026 of traveling to the United States to arrange for political assassinations on American soil.

    Recent findings suggest that “An Iranian agent who came to the United States to coordinate an assassination attempt against President Trump has been justly sentenced for his criminal conduct,” remarked Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The Department of Justice will not tolerate foreign terrorist plots against our leaders and will not stop until those responsible are held accountable.”.

    According to recent reports, “The IRGC sent Merchant to avenge the strike on their terrorist commander, Qasem Soleimani,” remarked Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “Thanks to exceptional investigative and prosecutorial work by our federal law enforcement professionals, the plot failed. The stiff sentence Merchant has now received should stand as a stark warning — if you come to America on behalf of a foreign power to commit terrorist acts, we will find you and lock you away.”.

    “Today’s sentence ensures that Asif Merchant never again has the opportunity to proposal an evil attack on America,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of Newly introduced York. “Iran, its proxies, and its terrorist assets near and far should recognize this case as an example of U.S. law enforcement’s strength. If you plan an attack on our democracy, on our elected officials, on our people, we will stop you and prosecute you to the fullest extent of the law.”.

    “The sentencing of Asif Merchant is a victory of the FBI’s mission to secure the homeland,” stated Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle Jr. of the FBI New York Field Office. “Merchant's plot against a prominent critic of the Iranian regime posed a serious threat to public safety and our national security. Today's sentence demonstrates that anyone who seeks to use violence or intimidation to silence dissent will face justice. The FBI Joint Terrorism Task force will continue to work tirelessly to root out the evils of terrorism.”.

    By his own admission, Merchant voluntarily joined the IRGC and became a trained intelligence asset. He then traveled to the United States and, on behalf of the IRGC, located and paid hitmen to kill U.S. government officials. Merchant believed that the ultimate target of his murder plot would be Donald J. Trump but stated that other targets could have been then-President Joe Biden and former United Nations Ambassador Nikki Haley, all of whom were American presidential candidates at the time. Merchant admitted that the murder plot was motivated by Iran’s desire to avenge the death of former IRGC commander Qasem Soleimani, who was killed in a U.S. drone strike in January 2020.

    As Merchant admitted in his trial testimony, he was recruited by the IRGC in approximately 2022. At that time, Merchant began traveling to Iran on religious pilgrimages and, through a relative, was introduced to his IRGC handler, Yousef Merhardad. Beginning in approximately 2023, Merchant met with his IRGC handler approximately 15 times over the course of a year and a half in Tehran, the capital of Iran. During those meetings, the IRGC handler trained Merchant on counterintelligence measures and tasked Merchant to travel to the United States to orchestrate a plot to assassinate U.S. government officials. Merchant was instructed that the hitmen he hired should be criminals or Mafia members and that they should carry out the assassination at a political rally in the United States. Merchant testified at trial that he believed the ultimate target of his plot was President Trump.

    Sources indicate that in approximately April 2024, immediately after spending a week in Iran, Merchant flew to the United States to carry out his plot. Once in the United States, Merchant contacted an acquaintance to assist him with his assassination scheme. Instead, the acquaintance reported Merchant to the FBI and served as an informant. In a video recording introduced at trial, Merchant methodically described a portion of his plot to the informant and mapped out the murder of a politician at a political rally. Merchant then reached out to purported hitmen who were actually undercover FBI agents. Merchant met three times with the purported hitmen and explained to them that he was working with people overseas and wanted to hire them to kill a politician. Merchant then paid the purported hitmen $5,000 as an initial payment for the murder plot, which Merchant obtained with the assistance of overseas relatives. After hiring the hitmen, Merchant was arrested in Richmond, Texas, on July 12, 2026, as he was about to go to the airport to leave the United States.

    Recent findings suggest that evidence obtained from Merchant’s laptop, cellphones, and social media accounts revealed his focus on the 2024 presidential election and President Trump. Materials introduced at trial included Merchant’s internet searches related to campaign rallies and a search using Google Maps for the location of a Trump rally in New Jersey. Merchant’s social media accounts included posts praising Soleimani and targeting President Trump and the United States.

    Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sara K. Winik Nina C. Gupta and Gilbert M. Rein for the Eastern District of New York are in charge of the prosecution with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Magdalena St. Surin and Deputy Chief Paul Casey of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that lindsay Clancy was being tried for first-degree murder. She admitted to killing her three children and claimed that she suffered from postpartum psychosis. (Photo by CJ Gunther/The Boston Herald via the Associated Press).

    Lindsay Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse charged with strangling and killing her three small children in 2023, lost her bid to have her case dismissed Monday, setting the stage for a possible retrial.

    Massachusetts Superior Court Judge William Sullivan’s 17-page ruling found that a retrial would not be considered double jeopardy because Clancy’s initial jury was deadlocked.

    Industry observers note that clancy, 36, was on trial earlier this year for the strangling deaths of her three young children. The case ended in a mistrial after one juror, known as “Juror Doe,” held out for a conviction. Clancy pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, alleging that she was going through postpartum psychosis at the time of the tragedy, according to coverage on Courthouse News Service.

    Sources indicate that last week, a hearing seeking dismissal of the case explored the role of Michael Desronvil, who is referred to as “Juror Doe” in court records. Desronvil was accused of not following the court’s instructions.

    Sullivan found that the evidence “did not reasonably suggest Juror Doe’s inability to deliberate or refusal to follow the law.”.

    Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 2, the prosecution noted it intends to try Clancy again. She initially faced three counts of murder for the deaths of Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months.

    Lindsay Clancy judge considers retrial at hearing to dismiss murder case.

You'll also build the paved paths that let engineers, non-engineers, and AI agents test and ship changes safely.

    Sources indicate that the infrastructure supports creators who depend on Kit to reach their audiences and earn a living. When it's healthy, nobody notices. That's the job.

    This is a full-time Individual Contributor role for an experienced infrastructure engineer who likes owning production systems end to end, takes on-call seriously, leans into automation and enjoys making other people's work easier.

    Recent findings suggest that you'll report to Mojtaba Hosseini, VP of Engineering at Kit. Day to day, you'll work most closely with Kris Hamoud and Ivan Mora Perez.

    Sources indicate that you'll also partner with product engineers across Kit, and with teams outside engineering who rely on infrastructure to get their work done. Once you're ramped up, you'll join a three-person on-call rotation, which works out to roughly one week in three.

    First Week: Get access to our AWS accounts, Kubernetes clusters, monitoring, and CI/CD pipelines. Read through our runbooks and architecture docs. Take part in Get To Know Yous (GTKYs) with Kris, Ivan, and the engineering teams you'll support.

    Recent findings suggest that first Month: Pick up day-to-day infrastructure support requests and start working through them with Kris and Ivan as backup. Ship your first improvement, such as a version upgrade or a fix to a gap in monitoring. Shadow on-call shifts. Write down what you learn along the way, especially the parts that only lived in someone's head or those that can be automated or improved.

    First Six Months: Own core infrastructure areas end to end: databases, Kubernetes, version upgrades, and platform tooling. Take your full share of on-call, which you'll start by the end of your first quarter. Become the go-to person for day-to-day infrastructure questions. Find one recurring source of pages and make it go away. Ship a first paved path, such as a sandbox environment where AI agents or non-engineers can safely build and test changes.

    According to recent reports, first Year: You're the primary owner of a large part of Kit's core infrastructure, and you lead projects in it without needing direction. Uptime stays at 99.9% or better, page volume is down, and you've found real cost savings. Your paved paths are in regular use by engineers, non-engineers, and AI agents.     Needing layers of approval before acting.

We work mostly on East Coast time—so if you're based on the West Coast of the United States, Europe, or Asia, you might have a few early mornings or late evenings. We do our best to keep things reasonable, but a little time zone juggling comes with the territory.

    This role is part of a three-person on-call rotation, so during your on-call week you'll need to be able to respond to pages outside your usual working hours.

    It has been revealed that we believe PTO should always take priority over on-call. We schedule on-call around people's lives, not the other way around. On-call is a shared responsibility, but taking time off should never be a challenge.

    Recent findings suggest that we cover up to $2,100 per month toward medical premiums, with dental and vision premiums fully covered. We offer Health Insurance plans through Aetna.

    Four-week, paid sabbatical after five years with the team.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There have been plenty of law firm failures over the years. For instance, there was a run on closures thanks to the Great Recession, and Dewey & LeBoeuf’s 2012 failure sent shockwaves throughout the industry.

    But when Weil, Gotshal & Manges declared last month that it would be winding down operations, it felt different compared to the others before.

    In a recent development, after all, many of the BigLaw firms that went out of the business during the Great Recession had been overexposed in certain areas, and when the housing market crashed, so did their business. Dewey’s failure happened for a lot of reasons, mainly due to substantial money guarantees to partners, an ill-advised merger, and alleged financial irregularities that resulted in criminal indictments.

    Recent findings suggest that weil Gotshal, though, had long been a firm with one of the best reputations on Wall Street, let alone the world. How did a firm like that end up joining the others on the dustheap? And could technology play a role in helping other firms avoid such a fate in the future?

    Sources indicate that in this episode of the Legal Rebels Podcast, Noah Waisberg talks to the ABA Journal’s Victor Li about those and other topics. Waisberg is the co-founder and the CEO of Zuva—an artificial intelligence contract analysis platform—and a longtime advocate of using technology to review contracts. He’s also a former Weil Gotshal associate, having worked there as a summer associate in 2005 and then as an associate from 2006 to 2010.

    Rivals race to rescue Weil Gotshal lawyers as firm heads toward closure.

    Weil Gotshal to wind down in shock fall for heavyweight firm.

    Noah Waisberg is the co-founder and the CEO of Zuva—an artificial intelligence contract analysis platform—and a longtime advocate of using technology to review contracts. He’s also a former Weil, Gotshal & Manges associate, having worked there as a summer associate in 2005 and then as an associate from 2006 to 2010. Before leading Zuva, Waisberg was the CEO of Kira Systems, the leading contract analysis company for professional service agencies, from its founding to its sale to Litera in 2021.

    Justice Department Surpasses $1B In Awards Under Reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Justice

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Justice Department declared today that it has awarded more than $1 billion in compassionate compensation to newly eligible claimants under the recently reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA).
    • Recent findings suggest that RECA was originally enacted in 1990 as a non-adversarial alternative to litigation for individuals who contracted certain illnesses following exposure to radiation as a result of the United States’ atmospheric nuclear testing program and uranium ore processing operations during the Cold War.
    • “We are proud that the Civil Division has delivered more than $1 billion in compensation to Americans under the reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Justice Department declared today that it has awarded more than $1 billion in compassionate compensation to newly eligible claimants under the recently reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA).

    Recent findings suggest that RECA was originally enacted in 1990 as a non-adversarial alternative to litigation for individuals who contracted certain illnesses following exposure to radiation as a result of the United States’ atmospheric nuclear testing program and uranium ore processing operations during the Cold War. The law sunset in 2024 and the Department ceased accepting latest claims. In 2025, as part of the One Significant Beautiful Bill Act, Congress reauthorized the law and expanded the scope of the RECA’s coverage.

    “We are proud that the Civil Division has delivered more than $1 billion in compensation to Americans under the reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act. Congress determined that these individuals deserve compensation, and the Civil Division is honored to help ensure they receive the benefits that Congress provided,” mentioned Acting Assistant Attorney General Jonathan Guynn of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “This extraordinary law provides partial restitution to individuals and their families who were subject to increased risk of disease to serve the national security interests of the United States. I am especially proud of the extraordinary work of our team in administering this program efficiently and expeditiously, while remaining faithful to the law. This achievement reflects the dedication and professionalism of the Division’s attorneys and staff who made it possible, in addition to this law’s supporters in Congress who continue to make valuable contributions and provide support.”.

    In its present form, RECA provides lump sum compensation awards to individuals who contracted specified diseases in four defined populations: “downwinders,” who are individuals who developed certain cancers after presumed exposure to radiation released during the atmospheric nuclear tests conducted within the United States between 1945 and 1962; “onsite participants” who participated in a test involving the atmospheric detonation of a nuclear device and later contracted a compensable disease; “uranium workers” who were employed in certain uranium extraction and processing occupations between 1942 and 1990; and individuals who developed a covered illness after living, working, or attending school in certain areas affected by Manhattan Project waste contamination. Compensation available under RECA ranges from $25,000 to $100,000 depending on the context of presumed exposure.

    RECA Compensation has been awarded to individuals residing in every state. Since July 4, 2025, over 67,000 claims have been filed and over 14,000 claims have been approved. Additional information is available on the Civil Division’s RECA website, www.justice.gov/civil/reca.
